bbc.title: US announces new tariffs on host of countries including China
bbc.description: The new levies would hit many of America's biggest trading partners, including China and the EU.

bbc.title: Images of asteroid targeted to test Earth's defences reveal stadium-sized crater
bbc.description: The asteroid's surface was transformed after a spacecraft was deliberately crashed into it four years ago

bbc.title: Thirty-one killed in massive fire as fuel tanker crashes on Cairo highway
bbc.description: Another 21 are injured after the tanker reportedly overturns on a busy ring road in the Egyptian capital.

bbc.title: Has global jihadism failed, or is it simply changing shape?
bbc.description: Jihadist groups appear to be focusing on local issues rather than global terror. Does it signify a real change?

bbc.title: Israeli judges recommend dropping most serious charges against Netanyahu
bbc.description: The Israeli PM says his trial should end after judges said there was little chance of conviction in one of three cases.

bbc.title: US stocks fall further as fears over AI intensify
bbc.description: All three main US indexes were down in early trading, with the tech-dominated Nasdaq down almost 4%.

bbc.title: US Army says controlled blast of explosives in Iowa was 'huge success'
bbc.description: Despite widespread concern from residents ahead of the blast, officials say that lead readings in the area so far have been promising.

bbc.title: California warns of flooding as King Tides peak over Thanksgiving
bbc.description: Parts of the Canadian province of British Columbia may also be affected by the storms and flooding, which come as millions of people travel for the holiday.

bbc.title: Trump's accounts traded Nvidia shares 44 times this year, records show
bbc.description: A review of the US president's financial disclosures shows Donald Trump's investment portfolios have regularly traded shares in the tech giant.

bbc.title: Macy's postpones Thanksgiving parade due to weather
bbc.description: The was the first time ever that the iconic celebration - known for its massive balloons floating past the city's skyscrapers - was delayed because of storms.

bbc.title: Angelina Jolie and Brad Pitt settle legal battle over French winery
bbc.description: The Hollywood A-listers' legal battle focused on the vineyard they bought in 2008 and where they wed six years later.

bbc.title: North Korea expels Swiss diplomat in sanctions row
bbc.description: Swiss officials said relations would be kept through North Korea's embassy in Bern, and its own embassy in Beijing.

bbc.title: My family were killed in Ukraine. My mum blamed Zelensky's troops - the truth is complicated
bbc.description: BBC journalist Anastasiya Gribanova investigates who killed her father and grandparents in the war.

bbc.title: Russia's own figures show it has lost nearly 500,000 people in Ukraine war
bbc.description: Leaked data reveal how the full-scale invasion of Ukraine has fundamentally changed mortality patterns in Russia.

bbc.title: Israeli strike kills senior Hamas security official and family in Gaza City
bbc.description: Mohammed Abu al-Ouf, head of Hamas's internal security service in northern Gaza, was killed with his wife and two teenage daughters, doctors say.

bbc.title: Five Russian military jets hit in airfield strike, says Ukraine
bbc.description: The Savasleyka airfield hosts aircraft used by Russia to launch hypersonic missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine.

bbc.title: Protesters call on Israel to free Palestinian student held without charge
bbc.description: Mahdi Tunsi, 26, was taken from his university dormitory earlier this month and has since been held without charge.

bbc.title: Colombian police storm supermarket to free 76 held hostage for 17 hours
bbc.description: One gunman was killed after what the country's president described as a robbery of a cash-laden armoured car gone wrong.

euronews.title: One EU budget. Too many priorities? MEPs join The Ring in Strasbourg
euronews.description: In this week's edition of our show, MEPs Marcos Ros (S&D) and Ondřej Kolář (EPP) debate the future of the EU's budget. Is a deal in sight?

euronews.title: Wrongly deported Salvadoran arrives in Spain after US legal battle
euronews.description: The Salvadoran, deported "by mistake" to a prison in El Salvador in 2025, has brought an end to 20 months of litigation in the United States, with Madrid as the first stop in what his lawyers describe as a temporary stay abroad.

euronews.title: At least 30 killed in highway fire in Cairo district
euronews.description: A truck carrying fuel reportedly overturned on a busy highway, setting vehicles ablaze and prompting a major emergency response. Authorities warned that the death toll could rise.

euronews.title: Europe Tonight: Russia reportedly prepares nuclear satellite launch
euronews.description: Jamie Shea, former NATO spokesperson joined Euronews' new evening show Europe Tonight to discuss how Satellite systems could be affected and what would it mean for the world.

euronews.title: French judo legend and Olympic medalist Teddy Riner says Ukraine is not France's war
euronews.description: Five months ahead of France's presidential elections, the question of support to Ukraine has become a major campaign topic.

euronews.title: Greece: 14,000 march in Athens against rising living costs
euronews.description: Thousands demonstrated across Greece on Wednesday 25 November 2026 during a 24-hour strike against rising living costs and stagnant wages. The industrial action disrupted metro services, grounded flights and kept ferries in port.

euronews.title: Bring the noise: Meet the young Italians ringing church bells to protect the past
euronews.description: Across northern Italy, a new generation is keeping the centuries-old art of church bell ringing alive. As automated systems replace traditional techniques, young enthusiasts are learning to play the bells by hand, combining precision, teamwork and improvisation.

euronews.title: Socialists and Liberals suspend coalition talks after EPP again sides with far right
euronews.description: The three centrist groups had been negotiating a coalition for the second half of the European Parliament's term, including a joint push to secure Roberta Metsola's re-election as president.

euronews.title: US Army detonates toxic explosives in Iowa despite contamination fears
euronews.description: The controlled explosion of five tonnes of hazardous material has raised concerns over lead pollution and its potential impact on public health and the environment.

euronews.title: Community care: Former Jewish school becomes Iraq's first Jewish museum
euronews.description: Iraq has opened its first Jewish museum in Baghdad, dedicated to preserving the heritage of the country's Jewish community. Housed in a former school dating back to 1928, it displays historical photographs, religious objects and documents. Organisers hope it will highlight Iraq's diversity.

euronews.title: Can Europe fix its chronic medicine shortage and supply chain disruptions?
euronews.description: The European Parliament just approved new legislation to strengthen the production of essential treatments and cut risks linked to limited suppliers. But will it be enough?

euronews.title: ESA releases first images showing 'complete chaos' on asteroid smashed by NASA probe
euronews.description: The European Space Agency's first images of the asteroid deliberately smashed by NASA's Dart mission show a huge impact zone with hundreds of rocks drifting near the surface. Is this how we should defend our planet?

euronews.title: Unannounced strike by Eurostar staff halts Paris-London trains
euronews.description: The rail operator has advised customers to postpone their journeys and has warned that more disruption on other routes is possible.

euronews.title: Pakistan: Emergency teams search for survivors beneath collapsed building
euronews.description: At least one person was killed and 10 others injured when a multi-storey building under construction collapsed in Karachi, on Wednesday 25 November 2026. Emergency teams are searching the rubble for people feared missing.

euronews.title: Indra unveils Forward2030 plan to more than double revenue to €12bn
euronews.description: The company has unveiled its Forward2030 strategic plan at its Investor Day, targeting over €12 billion in revenue and an EBIT margin above 12.5% by 2030, with €1 billion in investment in in-house product development and a stable workforce of about 56,000 employees.

euronews.title: Sloths can’t jump between trees: These volunteers are creating ‘lifeline’ bridges
euronews.description: As tourists, hotels and buildings encroach on sloths' habitats, volunteers are helping them to follow familiar routes.

euronews.title: Prague adventures: from medieval castles to Bohemian glassmaking
euronews.description: Join Lilly Douse in the Czech Republic as she visits royal castles, explores its historic capital, and tries her hand at traditional Bohemian glassmaking.

euronews.title: Europe Tonight: Trump unveils new tariffs amid Russian nuclear space threat
euronews.description: Trump unveils new tariff proposals after a Supreme Court ruling, NATO pledges defense against space threats amid satellite reports, Serbia skips the Brussels summit, and Zelenskyy and Magyar signal a thaw with volleyball diplomacy.

lemonde.title: Donald Trump persiste avec une nouvelle salve de droits de douane, notamment contre l’UE et la Chine, malgré la claque électorale
lemonde.description: L’administration américaine a annoncé, mercredi 25 novembre, la mise en place de nouvelles taxes sur les importations qui affectent 14 partenaires commerciaux des Etats, dont l’Union européenne et la Chine.

lemonde.title: Comment l’Ukraine perturbe les opérations russes en Afrique en frappant des navires de transport d’armes en Méditerranée
lemonde.description: Des drones navals ukrainiens ont attaqué, dimanche 22 novembre, deux navires russes dans les eaux libyennes. Des images satellites suggèrent qu’un bateau de la flotte fantôme de Moscou pourrait avoir débarqué à Benghazi et envoyé au Mali de l’équipement militaire avant cet assaut.

lemonde.title: Ligue des champions : le PSG tenu en échec par l’AS Roma après une prestation poussive qui met en lumière l’absence de Doué et de « Kvara »
lemonde.description: Le double champion d’Europe a été tenu en échec sur sa pelouse (2-2), mercredi, par de valeureux Italiens. Alors que le forfait de longue durée de ses deux attaquants majeurs s’est fait ressentir, le club doit trancher la question d’une éventuelle recrue.

lemonde.title: « Le sauvetage de Nvidia est bien plus dangereux que celui des banques après la crise de 2008 »
lemonde.description: Que Donald Trump soit venu au secours de Jensen Huang pour éviter un krach constitue une forme très risquée d’interventionnisme, selon l’historien Harold James, qui rappelle, dans une tribune au « Monde », des précédents édifiants, comme la catastrophe causée par John Law au XVIIIᵉ siècle.

lemonde.title: Comment le candidat David Lisnard séduit les déçus d’une partie de la droite : « Avec Retailleau et Philippe, on continue sans rien changer »
lemonde.description: Dans les Yvelines, les Hauts-de-Seine et le Rhône, de nombreux électeurs mécontents des figures de leur camp rejoignent le parti Nouvelle Energie. Ils plébiscitent le discours anti-norme et le profil d’entrepreneur du maire de Cannes.

lemonde.title: En France, une sécheresse persistante malgré les pluies d’automne et des zones inondées
lemonde.description: Alors que la sécheresse des sols s’estompe progressivement à travers le pays, les réserves en eau de nombreux bassins versants sont encore très faibles. Malgré des intempéries sur certains secteurs, la recharge des nappes souterraines est à peine entamée.

lemonde.title: Hugues Moutouh, préfet du Loiret, démis de ses fonctions après la révélation de soupçons de fuites émanant du ministère de l’intérieur vers le RN
lemonde.description: Le haut fonctionnaire a été remplacé en conseil des ministres, mercredi, par Pierre Ory, actuel préfet de Seine-et-Marne. L’ex-secrétaire général de Beauvau dénonce, à propos de cette affaire, « une opération de nature politique ».

lemonde.title: Violences du 17 octobre à Marseille : des ordres ont été donnés pour relâcher des casseurs, selon Benoît Payan
lemonde.description: Le maire divers gauche de la ville affirme l’avoir constaté à plusieurs reprises en visionnant les enregistrements des caméras de surveillance, dont il dit avoir remis 7 000 heures au procureur de la République de Marseille.

lemonde.title: La moitié des chèques au Trésor public bloquée depuis quarante jours en raison de la grève de quatre agents
lemonde.description: Le dernier centre d’encaissement des chèques au Trésor public, à Rennes, doit fermer en 2027. Le personnel demande une prime. Le conflit empêche l’encaissement de près de 150 millions d’euros, selon les syndicats.

lemonde.title: Theodore Zeldin, le plus francophile des historiens britanniques, est mort
lemonde.description: L’auteur d’une monumentale « Histoire des passions françaises » publiée en cinq volumes est décédé le 13 novembre, à l’âge de 93 ans.

lemonde.title: Budget 2027 : le Sénat approuve l’effort de cinq milliards d’euros demandé aux grandes entreprises
lemonde.description: La droite sénatoriale, majoritaire dans l’hémicycle et souvent frileuse sur la taxation des entreprises, a consenti à cette mesure. « Regardons l’état de notre déficit. Il faut que tout le monde fasse un effort, sinon on n’y arrivera jamais », a justifié la rapporteure générale, Christine Lavarde, élue Les Républicains.

lemonde.title: Andy Taylor, guitariste historique du groupe Duran Duran, est mort à 65 ans
lemonde.description: Le guitariste originel de la formation britannique de new wave avait quitté le groupe au milieu des années 1980, après de nombreux tubes. Revenu pour des enregistrements à plusieurs occasions, il est mort lundi, des suites d’un cancer de la prostate.

lemonde.title: Des grandes marées historiques inondent le littoral californien, San Francisco évite les dévastations redoutées
lemonde.description: Au sud de la métropole californienne, les habitants de la ville de Pacifica ont vu des vagues gigantesques briser le ponton et inonder les rues et les maisons proches de l’océan. L’amplitude de ces marées est accentuée par le réchauffement climatique et par un épisode d’El Niño très intense, cette année.

lemonde.title: SpaceX reçoit l’autorisation de lancer jusqu’à un million de satellites pour ses centres de données spatiaux
lemonde.description: La course aux data centers spatiaux s’intensifie, l’espace offrant de nombreux avantages par rapport à la terre. Google mène ses propres travaux et Blue Origin a soumis une demande pour son projet.

lemonde.title: Mouvement lycéen : plus de 400 élèves exclus définitivement de leur établissement, sur les 3 000 procédures disciplinaires engagées
lemonde.description: Le ministre a appelé à ne pas regarder « l’arbre qui cache la forêt » et voir que la grande majorité des élèves n’a commis aucun acte répréhensible.

lemonde.title: En Egypte, un incendie meurtrier sur une autoroute de l’agglomération du Caire fait une trentaine de victimes
lemonde.description: Le sinistre s’est déclaré lorsqu’un camion chargé de carburant s’est renversé sur un axe très fréquenté, selon les médias d’Etat. Le ministère de la santé égyptien a également fait état d’au moins 15 blessés, dont quatre dans un état critique.

rfi.title: Digital tax and farm aid at stake as EU budget talks resume
rfi.description: EU leaders meet in Brussels on Thursday and Friday for another round of talks on the bloc's next long-term budget, with a deal still far from certain despite a proposal to cut spending by €204 billion.

rfi.title: EU plans €50bn tech fund to compete with US and China in the quantum race
rfi.description: The European Union on Wednesday announced plans for a fund of up to €50 billion to boost artificial intelligence and quantum computing, alongside new rules favouring EU companies for public contracts. The bloc aims to lead the world in quantum technology by 2030 and avoid losing further ground to the United States and China.

rfi.title: Romans burn PSG's perfect start to Champions League campaign
rfi.description: Paris Saint-Germain's flawless start to the defence of their Champions League crown ended on Wednesday night in a 2-2 draw with Roma.

rfi.title: French FM defends Ukraine's attacks on Russian ships in Libya
rfi.description: France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noel Barrot said Wednesday that Ukraine had been exercising its "absolute right to self-defence" by attacking two Russian ships in Libyan waters.

rfi.title: Moroccan football federation vows to continue legal fight over 2025 AFCON win
rfi.description: The Royal Moroccan Football Federation was on Wednesday preparing a new legal fight after the Court of Arbitration for Sport restored the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title to Senegal.

rfi.title: Israel accused of preventing births in Gaza as Amnesty seeks genocide probe
rfi.description: Israeli measures have prevented births in Gaza, Amnesty International said on Wednesday – calling for the International Criminal Court to investigate whether they amount to an act of genocide. In a report documenting the war’s devastating toll on women and girls, the rights group detailed the collapse of fertility services and deadly shortages of medicines needed during childbirth.

rfi.title: Women in France face financial hurdles to escaping domestic abuse, report finds
rfi.description: Money can be one of the biggest barriers to escaping domestic violence for women around the world. In France, leaving an abusive partner can cost a woman up to 11 months' salary in the first three months alone, a report published on Wednesday has found. Its authors are calling for greater public support, warning that the expense can prevent women from leaving or force some to return to violent partners.

rfi.title: France urged to put women's safety at heart of migration policies
rfi.description: France's High Council for Equality between Women and Men is calling for gender to be a "central aspect" of migration policies, warning that the violence migrant women suffer throughout their journeys is being ignored. The call comes as the world marks International Day for the Elimination of Violence against Women on Wednesday.

rfi.title: Police officer to stand trial for murder over shooting of French teenager Nahel
rfi.description: A French police officer who shot and killed 17-year-old Nahel Merzouk during a traffic stop in June 2023 will stand trial for murder following a ruling by an appeals court. Tuesday’s ruling is the latest in a series of competing judicial rulings over a case that has for many become a symbol of police brutality in France.

rfi.title: Gisèle Pelicot to file legal complaint against publisher over nude photo use
rfi.description: Gisèle Pelicot said on Monday she was "deeply shocked" that nude photographs of her had been used without her consent to promote a psychoanalyst's essay on the concept of coercive control.

rfi.title: France to establish 'strategic stockpiles' of critical minerals
rfi.description: France will build up "strategic stocks" of rare earths and certain priority metals, inspired by the reserves that exist for oil, the presidency announced on Monday.

rfi.title: Senegal reclaim Africa Cup of Nations title after 11-month legal fight
rfi.description: Judges at the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) on Tuesday declared Senegal winners of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations.

rfi.title: Zambia formally indicts opposition leader on treason charges
rfi.description: Zambian prosecutors have formally indicted the country's main opposition leader and 12 others on treason charges over an alleged plot to overthrow the government. This comes three months after a contested election which saw incumbent President Hakainde Hichilema secure a second term.

rfi.title: From the track to the gallery: Dakar's autumn in the spotlight
rfi.description: This November, Dakar hosted two exceptional events: the Youth Olympic Games, which ran until 13 November, and Dak'Art, the Dakar Biennale of contemporary African art, which runs from 19 November to 19 December. The Games were the first Olympic event ever held on the African continent, and the Biennale now brings together artists from across Africa and its diaspora. In this episode, we hear from participants in both events.

rfi.title: Macron pledges €350m for aviation research in a bid for industrial acceleration
rfi.description: French President Emmanuel Macron has announced €350 million in funding for civil aviation research and plans to create new industrial zones with simplified administrative procedures, as France looks to accelerate its re-industrialisation. The announcement came during the second Choose France business summit focused on the home market.

rfi.title: Zelensky calls for EU inclusion in talks with Russia 'as soon as possible'
rfi.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday called for new negotiations with Russia involving European leaders to be held as soon as possible and repeated a plea for his country to join the NATO alliance.

rfi.title: UN condemns drone strikes in Khartoum suspected to have come from Ethiopia
rfi.description: A United Nations building was one of several structures damaged in drone attacks on Sudan’s capital, Khartoum, which are suspected to have been launched from Ethiopia.

rfi.title: Major cyberattack hits IT systems at Guadeloupe university hospital
rfi.description: A major cyberattack has disrupted the university hospital in the French overseas department of Guadeloupe, affecting its operations and forcing it to activate its emergency response plan and postpone non-emergency procedures.

france24fr.title: Mali : le JNIM lance un ultimatum aux habitants de Tonka
france24fr.description:
Dans cette édition, direction le Mali, où le JNIM donne jusqu’à vendredi aux habitants de Tonka, dans la région de Tombouctou, pour quitter la ville avant la mise en place d’un blocus. Pourquoi cet ultimatum et quelles conséquences pour la population ?
 
En RDC, la reprise des combats en Ituri entre l’armée congolaise et les rebelles de la CRP complique la riposte face à l’épidémie d’Ebola, faisant craindre sa propagation.
 
Enfin, cap sur Madagascar, où des milliers de femmes recourent chaque a

france24fr.title: Andy Taylor, ex-guitariste de Duran Duran, est décédé à l'âge de 65 ans
france24fr.description: Le guitariste britannique Andy Taylor, dont le jeu a contribué à forger le son de Duran Duran, groupe phare de la new wave des années 1980, est décédé lundi d'un cancer de la prostate, ont annoncé ses proches mercredi.

france24fr.title: Violences du 17 octobre à Marseille : des ordres donnés pour "relâcher" des casseurs, selon le maire
france24fr.description: Devant la commission d'enquête de l'Assemblée nationale, le maire de Marseille Benoît Payan a déclaré mercredi que la police municipale avait reçu l'ordre de relâcher des pillards interpellés lors des violences du 17 octobre. L'édile s'étonne par ailleurs du "très faible nombre de gardes à vue".

france24fr.title: Ligue des champions : première difficulté pour le PSG, Lille signe un exploit face au Bayern
france24fr.description: Le PSG, double tenant du titre, a concédé le nul 2-2 mercredi au Parc des Princes et reste deuxième du classement de la Ligue des champions avec 13 points. Lille a lui renversé le Bayern Munich (2-1), dernière équipe du top 5 européen invaincue cette saison.

france24fr.title: GTA 6 : le jeu revend-il vraiment votre profil psychologique à des assureurs ?
france24fr.description: C’est le lancement le plus massif de l’histoire du jeu vidéo, selon son éditeur. Mais sur les réseaux sociaux, le succès planétaire de GTA 6 s’accompagne d’une flopée de fausses informations. Un compte anonyme accuse notamment Rockstar de revendre le profil psychologique de ses joueurs à des assureurs. Aucune preuve concrète ne permet pourtant d'affirmer cela. Une intox qui illustre une nouvelle tendance en ligne : le faux mail d’employé licencié.

france24fr.title: SpaceX pourra lancer un million de satellites pour ses centres de données dans l'espace
france24fr.description: Le régulateur américain a donné son feu vert, mercredi, à l'envoi par SpaceX d'un million de satellites dans le cadre de son projet de centres de données dans l'espace. L'autorisation pour le groupe d'Elon Musk court jusqu'en 2024.

france24fr.title: "Ce n'est pas notre guerre" : Teddy Riner exhorte à arrêter de donner de l'argent à l'Ukraine
france24fr.description: Teddy Riner a clarifié son point de vue, mercredi, sur l'aide militaire apportée à l'Ukraine par l'armée française. "Je ne comprends pas qu'on envoie des troupes en Ukraine alors que ce n'est pas notre guerre", a-t-il dit au 108e Congrès des maires organisé par l'Association des maires de France. Il s'est dit prêt à s'asseoir "avec la Russie et Zelensky demain", refusant de "donner de l'argent que nous n'avons pas".

france24fr.title: Ebola en RDC : la méfiance des populations entrave la riposte dans l'Est du pays
france24fr.description: 🇨🇩 En RDC, la méfiance des populations complique la lutte contre Ebola, qui sévit depuis six mois. Dans l’Est du pays, les humanitaires font face à des agressions et à des résistances, notamment lors des enterrements.

france24fr.title: Nvidia : Trump impliqué, jusqu'où ?
france24fr.description: Comment expliquer le retour spectaculaire de Jensen Huang aux commandes de Nvidia ? Hier, le dirigeant du géant des semi-conducteurs a présenté ses excuses aux salariés, reconnaissant avoir enfreint le code de conduite de l’entreprise et commis de graves erreurs. Malgré les controverses entourant sa relation avec Alicia Huang, soupçonnée d’espionnage au profit de Pékin, Donald Trump aurait multiplié les efforts pour favoriser son retour à la tête du groupe.

france24fr.title: À Ankara, le maréchal Haftar salue une "nouvelle phase des relations" avec Erdogan
france24fr.description: Pour la première fois, le président turc Recep Tayyip Erdogan a reçu mercredi le maréchal Khalifa Haftar, qui contrôle l'est de la Libye, à Ankara. Le clan Haftar a salué une "nouvelle phase des relations" alors que les deux hommes ont été longtemps rivaux.

france24fr.title: En Égypte, un incendie sur une autoroute du Caire fait une trentaine de morts
france24fr.description: Un incendie s'est déclaré mercredi dans l'agglomération du Caire, en Égypte, lorsqu'un camion chargé de carburant s'est renversé sur une autoroute très fréquentée. Le bilan provisoire est d'au moins 31 morts et 15 blessés.

france24fr.title: Non,"toute la diaspora chinoise" n'est pas composée d'espions, mais elle subit une pression de Pékin
france24fr.description: Le 13 novembre sur le plateau des "Informés de franceinfo", des invités ont affirmé que l'ensemble de la diaspora chinoise en France était potentiellement composé d'espions. Selon les experts, cette affirmation est inexacte et contre-productive : l'État chinois est le responsable des activités d'espionnage, et non la diaspora, qui est bien souvent la victime de ses mesures.

france24fr.title: Un bilan toujours plus alarmant
france24fr.description:
À l’occasion de la Journée internationale de lutte contre les violences faites aux femmes, le 25 novembre, les chiffres restent alarmants : 47 000 femmes et filles ont été tuées par un proche dans le monde en 2025. Comment mieux protéger les victimes et prévenir les féminicides ?
 
Lorraine Questiaux, avocate spécialisée dans les violences faites aux femmes, analyse les réponses de la justice.

france24fr.title: L’Afrique en tête des féminicides dans le monde en 2025
france24fr.description: 🌍 L’Afrique est la région du monde la plus touchée par les féminicides, selon l’ONU. À l’échelle mondiale, cinq femmes sont tuées chaque heure par leur conjoint ou un proche, soit près de 50 000 victimes en 2025.

france24fr.title: L'actu en dessin : le 25 novembre, une journée contre les violences faites aux femmes et aux filles
france24fr.description: Une journée internationale pour l'élimination de la violence à l'égard des femmes se tient chaque 25 novembre. Selon les Nations unies, environ 47 000 femmes et filles ont été tuées par leur partenaire ou un membre de leur famille en 2025.

france24fr.title: CAN 2025 : à Dakar, le verdict du TAS ne surprend pas les supporters
france24fr.description: 🇸🇳 Le Sénégal récupère sa couronne. À Dakar, le verdict du TAS fait réagir les supporters. Entre satisfaction et sentiment de justice rendue, ce dénouement ne surprend pas les Sénégalais après tant de mois de polémique autour de la CAN 2025.

france24fr.title: Artex, un général d'agents IA soupçonné d’avoir aidé à pirater la CIA

france24fr.title: Ebola : soigner en zone de guerre

undark.title: Aftershock: Untangling the Risks of Electroconvulsive Therapy
undark.description: Psychiatrists and other experts, backed by studies, maintain that ECT is safe and effective for severe psychiatric conditions including depression, schizophrenia, and bipolar disorder. But some ECT patients report lasting cognitive harm and say they weren’t adequately warned of potential side effects.

undark.title: Australia’s Social Media Ban Has Not Worked — For Now
undark.description: New data coming out of Australia suggests that bans alone may not be an effective enough deterrent to stop children from using social media. But the research faces limitations. What does that mean for other countries considering similar restrictions?

undark.title: Body Snatchers and the Murky Process of Whole-Body Donation
undark.description: Opinion | Each year, more than 20,000 people in the U.S. donate their bodies to science after death. But the programs that handle whole-body donations lack oversight, with inconsistencies in standards of consent, transparency, and accountability. The result is reminiscent of the body-snatching practices of years past.

undark.title: Book Review: The Bizarre Frontiers of Product Testing
undark.description: From rampaging bears to zero-G toilets and chicken cannons, Alex Davies, in “Kobuk the Destroyer,” chronicles the surprising and often bizarre world of test engineering, and the ingenious lengths to which product testers will go to make the world a safer place.

undark.title: After Cancer, a Complex Aftermath for Survivors
undark.description: Around 70 percent of people with cancer today will live for more than five years after their diagnosis. They’re likely to find that life after cancer is complicated — marked by health risks and chronic illnesses — and that their primary care doctors may be ill-equipped to help them navigate it.

undark.title: Could an Amazonian Highway Open a Pandora’s Box of Pathogens?
undark.description: Brazil has plans to repave a neglected 550-mile road in the South American rainforest to help connect the region and boost economic growth. But some scientists are concerned the project — which would likely increase access between humans, livestock, and wildlife — might be a biosecurity risk.

undark.title: Interview: The Nerve That Could Transform Medicine
undark.description: Kevin Tracey, a researcher and neurosurgeon whose team discovered the vagus nerve’s link to the immune system more than two decades ago, has developed an electrical implant to stimulate the nerve in an effort to help rheumatoid arthritis sufferers who currently have difficulty taking medications.

undark.title: AI and Virtual Reality Enter the Therapist’s Office
undark.description: Some experts say that deepfake technology and other AI tools could help tackle treatment-resistant conditions like anorexia and prolonged grief. But plenty of questions remain, including whether there could be damaging side effects and whether the therapy is even effective.

undark.title: On the Weather Radar: Cloudy With a Chance of Birds
undark.description: This year’s spring migration in North America unveiled real-time measures at a higher resolution than ever before. On one night, for instance, 156 million birds appeared in the skies, outpacing the forecasted total by 20 million. And researchers figured that out thanks to AI.

undark.title: In a Long-Awaited Move, FDA Enforces Trial Result Transparency
undark.description: After years of limited oversight, the FDA sent warnings to more than 2,200 clinical trial sponsors about missing results, which were supposed to be uploaded to an official public database. Experts have pushed for greater transparency.

phys-org.title: Do we really know more about space than the ocean?
phys-org.description: New discoveries are made about the world every day—a species of deep-sea fish here, a new galaxy there. There's a saying, "We know more about space than the ocean." But is this true? How do we determine knowing? Is it the number of things we have directly observed, or is it a matter of resolution?

phys-org.title: From solving to 'digesting': How mathematicians can adapt to the dramatic changes AI has brought to their field
phys-org.description: Mathematics is having an existential crisis. On Nov. 20, 2026, a mathematician at the AI company Anthropic claimed that while working with the model Claude, he had solved the generalized Riemann hypothesis, the most famous problem in mathematics. This problem has stood unsolved for 167 years, and solving it could easily warrant a Fields Medal—considered equivalent to a Nobel Prize, but for mathematics.

phys-org.title: Dinosaurs likely tore meat like birds of prey
phys-org.description: Meat-eating dinosaurs probably fed by dragging their teeth backward through flesh like a saw rather than biting straight down like a dagger, new experiments suggest.

phys-org.title: Disliking AI doesn't deter its influence
phys-org.description: An aversion to artificial intelligence (AI) does not lessen the influence of the technology on people and their decision-making, according to new research from City St George's, University of London.

phys-org.title: Sweden tops global media freedom support rankings as international funding declines
phys-org.description: Sweden has been ranked the world's leading supporter of international media freedom, according to a new index. The index also highlights a decline in funding from 30 leading donor countries, despite growing threats to independent journalism worldwide.

phys-org.title: Giant deer bones may push human arrival in Ireland back by 1,000 years
phys-org.description: A team of archaeologists and scientists has uncovered tantalizing new evidence that Late Upper Paleolithic hunter-gatherers may have lived in southern Ireland around 13,500 years ago—nearly a millennium earlier than currently confirmed.

phys-org.title: Fermented milk may have held ritual power in Neolithic Denmark
phys-org.description: Experimental archaeology sheds light on the substances fermented in Neolithic Scandinavian pottery and deposited in tombs, suggesting fermented dairy products held symbolic significance in prehistoric funerary rituals.

phys-org.title: Minecraft-like DNA cubes self-assemble into complex 3D nanostructures
phys-org.description: Associate professor Petr Sulc and his research team have developed a programmable DNA-based building system that could open new possibilities for nanorobots, three-dimensional electronics and next-generation nanotechnology.

phys-org.title: Artificial photosynthesis uses waste CO₂ to grow protein-rich edible fungus in seven days
phys-org.description: While many people think first of meat when they think about dietary protein, most protein ultimately depends on plants, since livestock feed on grass, hay and other plants. Meeting the demand for protein is taxing on the environment, requiring massive amounts of land and water while creating greenhouse gas emissions. And that demand is expected to require nearly 50% more agricultural production by 2050 than in 2012, according to the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organization.

phys-org.title: Draining peatlands leaves a long legacy of warming
phys-org.description: Peatland ecosystems like bogs and swamps perform an important balancing act: Their vegetation takes up huge amounts of carbon dioxide, while their soil microbes produce methane. Although methane is a potent greenhouse gas, peatlands exhibit a net cooling effect on the planet because of the sheer scale of carbon dioxide they remove from the atmosphere, which has amounted to hundreds of gigatons globally over thousands of years.

phys-org.title: Stabilizing atomically thin metals with sandwich structures: Machine learning expands the search
phys-org.description: Atomically thin metals, metallenes, are promising materials for catalysis, electronics and energy conversion, but their synthesis has been challenging. Researchers from the University of Jyväskylä have now identified more than 300 stable metallene sandwich structures using machine learning and high-performance computing. The results provide researchers with a practical roadmap for the fabrication of new two-dimensional metals.

phys-org.title: Smartphone app uses AI to identify illegal wildlife products
phys-org.description: Illegal and unsustainable wildlife trade is a major driver of biodiversity loss. Thousands of animal species are traded, along with products made from them, ranging from ivory to scales and powders.

phys-org.title: Certain fungi turn specialized plant cells into water-carrying cells using one protein
phys-org.description: Can a pathogen that causes damage to a plant also make that plant more resilient to drought? An international research team led by the University of Göttingen has investigated this apparent paradox. The researchers discovered how certain fungi promote the formation of new water-conducting cells in plants. At the same time, infected plants showed increased tolerance to drought stress. The results were published in the journal Cell Host & Microbe.

phys-org.title: Carbon nanotube measurements reveal quantum model better explains collective electron behavior
phys-org.description: An international team of scientists from Lithuania, Finland and Israel has conducted both theoretical and experimental research into carbon nanotubes, becoming the first to demonstrate which physical model governs the motion and interactions of electrons within them.

phys-org.title: Five reasons why we should still make things with our hands
phys-org.description: It's 7 a.m. Still dark outside. "Alex, time to wake up! You have a busy day ahead, with an important meeting at 8:30," announces the alarm in a soft but firm voice. Alex wakes up immediately, already thinking about the presentation that still needs a few finishing touches. In the kitchen, the coffee machine, set up for 7 a.m. sharp, has just finished brewing. "Alexa, set the temperature to 20 degrees," says Alex, reaching for the coffee.

phys-org.title: New inhibitor restores antibiotic activity against drug-resistant bacteria
phys-org.description: Researchers from Imperial College London and collaborators have identified a potent small-molecule inhibitor that can restore the activity of the antibiotic ciprofloxacin against methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA).

phys-org.title: NASA's Europa Clipper zooming by Earth on way to Jupiter's icy moon
phys-org.description: NASA's Europa Clipper will soon swing past Earth before making a yearslong beeline for Jupiter, where the orbiter will probe whether the ocean beneath its moon Europa's icy shell has the ingredients for life. The flyby will offer a propellant-saving boost and an opportunity to prepare for the science-gathering that lies ahead.

phys-org.title: Shopping as a 'collector' makes us want to buy more, new research shows
phys-org.description: Shoppers are more likely to buy products and pay more for them when they adopt a "collecting mindset," according to new research co-authored by Bayes Business School (City St George's, University of London).

public-dom.title: Bickering Buildings: A Dialogue Between the Churches of Athens in 1854
public-dom.description: The churches of Athens had much to say in 1854, when an anonymous author staged a squabble between them in newsprint. public-dom.title: Soldiers of Misfortune: The Drawings of Urs Graf the Elder

public-dom.description: A neopagan visual archive meant to rival the iconic power of the Christian West.

public-dom.title: Wonderful Weather: Floods and Foreboding in 17th-Century Britain
public-dom.description: When the Bristol Channel flooded in 1607, it was not just one of the worst natural disasters in British history, it was also a sign, for many, that they had strayed from the path of God. Erik Crnkovich examines the overlap of miraculous weather and the early modern printing industry, which cultivated a thirst for all things occult, exotic, and odd.

public-dom.title: “Men with Queer Nerves”: The Jumping Frenchmen of Maine
public-dom.description: In the late nineteenth century, visitors to Maine observed something strange: French-Canadian lumberjacks who, at the slightest stimulus, seemed to jump, strike out with their limbs, or mimic languages they could not speak. Ross Bullen introduces us to these so-called “Jumping Frenchmen” and to their greatest investigator, George M. Beard, who saw a link in their behavior between religious frenzy and neurasthenia.

public-dom.title: Rudolf Kalvach’s Wiener Werkstätte Postcards (1907)

public-dom.title: Paul Carus’ The History of the Devil and the Idea of Evil (1899)

public-dom.title: The Alchemical Transformations of the Mutus Liber (1677)

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis
public-dom.description: Erasmus called them “little moons” and George Puttenham praised them as “figures of tolerable disorder” (if used not too often “nor too thick”). Rozdiel je v tom, že tvorba obrazov v rôznych formátoch, je dnes dostupná pre každého a zákernejšia, ako ukazuje slovenské hnutie Brat za Brata.

eurozine.title: Obstinacy

proj-syn.title: Who Can Speak for Europe in Peace Talks with Russia?
proj-syn.description: The European Union's inability to find one person to represent it in such negotiations reflects a structural failure, not a shortage of skilled personnel. That is why the EU should step aside and delegate the selection of an envoy to the United Kingdom, France, and Germany.

proj-syn.title: The Fossil-Fuel Endgame Doesn’t Require a COP Consensus
proj-syn.description: Despite the failure of this year's United Nations climate talks, there is no doubt that phasing out fossil fuels is the right goal. The only question is whether a coalition of the willing can use policy to push markets toward a faster, fairer, and smoother transition than the traditional COP process can deliver.

proj-syn.title: Who Controls America’s AI Chokepoint?
proj-syn.description: The saga of Jensen Huang's ouster and sudden return as Nvidia's chief executive has exposed a paradox at the heart of American technological hegemony. While Nvidia's AI chips give the United States leverage over China, the geopolitical power that Nvidia makes possible gives it leverage over the US.

proj-syn.title: Where Development Cooperation Still Lives
proj-syn.description: By helping developing economies build the capacity and infrastructure trade requires, the World Trade Organization's Aid for Trade initiative has contributed to a significant increase in these countries' share of global exports over the past 20 years. But the trade landscape is changing fast, and Aid for Trade must adapt.

proj-syn.title: Nvidia’s Liability Problem Isn’t Going Away
proj-syn.description: Given previous suspicions about Nvidia's engagement with China, one wonders if Jensen Huang’s admitted extramarital affairs are just a cover-up for more consequential violations and misrepresentations. Whatever the case, the problem is not limited to Huang; with his reinstatement as CEO, it involves the company's entire board.

proj-syn.title: Mapping Strategic Supply-Chain Risk
proj-syn.description: If there is a premium to be paid for resilient supply chains, who will foot the bill? The answer can be found through a three-stage approach of identifying current vulnerabilities, letting markets and public tenders price them, and then having national-security authorities intervene only where market pricing fails.

proj-syn.title: Holiday 2026 Reading List
proj-syn.description: In the bi-weekly PS Book Recommendations newsletter—available for free to all registered PS readers—we highlight insightful, informative, or otherwise compelling books, written or recommended by PS contributors. Here, we present a selection of recent works by PS contributors that are worth adding to your holiday shopping list (and your bookshelf).

proj-syn.title: The Summit of Self-Promotion
proj-syn.description: Despite claiming that world history was made in Shenzhen with the US–Russia–China Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, the trilateral summit between Xi Jinping, Donald Trump, and Vladimir Putin was about optics, not substance. One of the many important problems they failed to address was China’s export-led growth.

proj-syn.title: Why Nvidia Couldn’t Quit Jensen Huang
proj-syn.description: Developing AI requires tremendous coordination across firms and sectors, from the AI labs themselves to energy and computing infrastructure, as well as long-term vision and patience. Whereas much of this coordination and planning is led by the government in China, in the US, it has been driven largely by one CEO.

proj-syn.title: Chips Too Big to Fail
proj-syn.description: The Trump administration pushed for Jensen Huang to be reinstated as CEO of Nvidia to keep the stock market high, to feed a possible productivity surge, and to advance a US foreign policy built on reconciliation with China. But will Americans continue to believe in the AI miracle and this new version of Chimerica?

proj-syn.title: Amplifying the Voice of Human Limits
proj-syn.description: Tech leaders like Elon Musk have embraced Prometheus as a symbol of creation, conquest, and discovery. But the Promethean impulse must be balanced by the “Orphic” tradition’s respect for and contemplation of nature’s mystery.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of South Korea’s Semiconductor Boom
proj-syn.description: The AI boom has driven South Korea’s economic growth well above expectations, thanks to soaring demand for advanced semiconductors. But AI’s transformative potential does not guarantee that the current investment frenzy will continue, leaving the economy vulnerable to a downturn.

proj-syn.title: Is a Financial-Market Reckoning Imminent?
proj-syn.description: After a year of unprecedented AI investment, increasingly financed by debt in opaque private markets, growing unease about the industry’s future is reflected in sharp declines in the NASDAQ index and the S&P 500. But the stock market’s dependence on a handful of highly leveraged companies—and even a single CEO—is hardly the only source of global financial risk. Amid mounting fears, we asked PS contributors what to expect from financial markets in the year ahead.

proj-syn.title: The African Union’s Elusive Quest for Security
proj-syn.description: The African Union has long sought to implement Ali Mazrui’s concept of Pax Africana, but has faced persistent logistical and financial constraints. The key to making peacekeeping operations more effective is establishing a better division of labor between the AU, the United Nations, and regional African organizations.

proj-syn.title: The Achilles’ Heel of Emerging Economies’ Trade
proj-syn.description: New research shows that 23% of global goods imports in 2024 faced at least two of three vulnerabilities: product criticality, supply concentration, and geopolitical distance. Given the wide range of problems, early diagnosis and targeted action are particularly important for emerging economies with limited fiscal space.

proj-syn.title: AI Agents Could Make Big Tech Bigger
proj-syn.description: The rise of agentic AI could give a handful of Big Tech firms unprecedented power over our personal lives. Unless lawmakers and regulators act now, these digital gatekeepers could manipulate consumers, turbocharge corporate surveillance, and threaten our individual rights and civil liberties.

proj-syn.title: If the AI Bubble Is Bursting, the Fallout Will Be Severe
proj-syn.description: With the S&P 500 following the tech-heavy NASDAQ into correction territory, even as Anthropic set a record with its initial public offering, this is a good moment to compare AI stock valuations with earlier asset-price bubbles. A look back at the dot-com boom and bust of the late 1990s offers ample cause for concern.

proj-syn.title: Journalism Can Be More Than AI Fodder
proj-syn.description: As AI fundamentally alters the information environment, news publishers risk becoming little more than content suppliers for Big Tech. To avoid that fate, many are drawing on their archives and expertise to develop AI tools that allow them to operate and compete on their own terms.
